messages:
Maya: FYI customer (Vertico Health) asked if we can do a fully air-gapped POC and what the packaging/upgrade cadence would look like. They also care about SBOM + signed bundles.
Rafael: Short answer: yes. We support an offline installer bundle + optional delta patches. Need to confirm model set size and whether they want daily security patches vs quarterly model updates.
Maya: They want security patches monthly, model updates quarterly. Network is strict: inbound only via secure SFTP from their jump host, no registry access.
Priya: For security checklist: we provide a signed bundle (RSA256), SBOM, and reproducible build hashes. We require customer to validate signatures with our public key. Can support offline attestation docs.
Anya: Upgrade cadence we recommend: monthly critical OS/security hotfix bundles, quarterly model/feature bundles. We can do emergency hotfixes in between but they’re full bundles unless the fix is tiny.
Eli: Implementation notes: bundles are tar.gz with installer + runtime + model artifacts. Typical sizes: base runtime ~2GB, each large model 4-12GB depending on quantization. Full bundle for a stack with 2 models ~10-20GB.
Rafael: We also support delta patching for configs and small binary patches (~<200MB). Large model swaps are full downloads. Delta mechanism is rsync-like; customer can apply with our `redwood-offline` CLI.
Maya: Can we do signed delta patches? customer asked about chain-of-trust.
Priya: Yes — deltas are signed. They get a YAML manifest + signature. Also provide SBOM snapshots per bundle. Key rotation is supported but must be coordinated (offline exchange of new public key).
Eli: Example install command they can run on the air-gapped host: ```
redwood-offline install --bundle redwood-bundle-2026-03-01.tar.gz --verify-signature /opt/redwood
```
Rafael: For pull options: we can deliver via SFTP or ship an encrypted USB image. We also support an internal staging registry mirrored by customer if they run an internal registry behind the jump host.
Maya: They asked about telemetry — we must confirm what we collect and how to disable.
Priya: Telemetry is opt-in for air-gapped installs. Default is disabled. We provide a manual telemetry toggles doc and an on-prem metrics-exporter that can push to customer MDM if they allow.
Anya: Operationally we’ll include: preflight checks, node-level driver compatibility checklist (NVIDIA driver CUDA versions), rollback steps, and validation tests for model inference.
Eli: Note on GPUs: quantized runtime needs specific CUDA+cuDNN combos. We'll supply a compatibility matrix and a small sanity test (perf + accuracy).
Maya: Next steps for POC: 1) Send SBOM + public signing key; 2) Schedule 1-node POC runbook review w/ops; 3) Confirm which models they want in the bundle.
Rafael: I’ll generate a minimal POC bundle (runtime + one quantized model) and a delta patch example. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Priya: I’ll attach the security questionnaire answers and instructions for offline key exchange in the repo.
deploy-bot: bundle-build/1934567901 completed: redwood-bundle-2026-03-01.tar.gz (sha256: abcd...ef12) :white_check_mark:
Maya: Great — I’ll follow up with Vertico and book the runbook call. Thanks all :thumbsup:
